verdict.rationale: Each Superpowers skill ships as a plain, human-readable SKILL.md that is itself documentation of the behavior it enforces (e.g. the TDD skill's rule). The using-superpowers skill documents some activation routing, such as 'Fix this bug' leading to systematic-debugging, so developers can inspect behavior before it runs. However, skills trigger automatically, and the evidence does not show that every skill carries an explicit description of its activation conditions. Missing for 10: proof that every skill documents a 'when it activates' trigger or description field, a per-skill catalog of activation conditions, and independent corroboration that the behavior is predictable.

support.subject: As a developer, every skill documents what it does and when it activates, so I can predict my agent's new behavior before it surprises me

citations.quote: Skills are plain, selectively-installable markdown folders.
the installer prints 'Review skills before use; they run with full agent permissions.'
"Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
